title: Which number between one and ten is perfect?
description: A perfect number has factors that add up to twice the number. Testing the numbers from two to nine, adding their factors each time, shows which one is perfect.
teaching_notes: One idea: add all the factors of a number, including one and the number itself, and compare with twice the number. Watch for students who leave out the number itself.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q3, p.111
video_script.why: The child adds all the factors of each number from two to nine and compares the total with twice the number.
video_script.substitution: List all the factors of a number, add them, and compare with twice the number.
video_script.anchor: the perfect number 28 with its factors added to fifty six
video_script.payoff_line: The perfect number between one and ten is six

final_answer.spoken: the perfect number between one and ten is six

video_script.design: One idea: add every factor, including one and the number, and compare with twice the number. Same method as the book example: factors in pairs.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the number 28 with its factors 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28 and their sum 56

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.def: the words perfect number appear beside 28
marks.ex: the factors of 28 are added to 56 and 2 x 28 = 56 is written
marks.ask: a number strip from 1 to 10 appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a perfect number.
<bookmark mark='def'/>A number is called a perfect number when all its factors add up to twice the number.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Twenty eight is perfect, because its factors add up to fifty six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find a perfect number between one and ten?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number with all its factors added, the total compared with twice the number

marks.way: the example from the book is pointed to
marks.all: the factors of one number are added in a row
marks.twice: the total is joined to 2 x the number

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Add every factor of a number, including one and the number itself.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>The total must be twice the number.
<bookmark mark='test'/>We test the numbers from two to nine.

beats.on_screen: Given: a perfect number has the sum of all its factors equal to twice the number; look between 1 and 10

marks.given: the rule and the range are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the factors must add up to twice the number, and the number lies between one and ten.

beats.on_screen: To find: a perfect number between 1 and 10

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a number in this range that obeys the rule.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 2 has 1, 2 sum 3; 3 has 1, 3 sum 4; 4 has 1, 2, 4 sum 7; 5 has 1, 5 sum 6; twice is 4, 6, 8, 10: none fits

marks.sums: the factors of 2, 3, 4 and 5 are added and the sums are written
marks.twice: 2 x each number is written and each pair gets a cross

narration: <bookmark mark='sums'/>Step one, try two, three, four and five. Their factors add up to three, four, seven and six.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Twice each number is four, six, eight and ten, so none of them fits.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 6 has 1, 2, 3, 6; the sum is 12, which is 2 x 6
narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step two, try six. Its factors are one, two, three and six.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>They add up to twelve, which is twice six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 7 sum 8, 8 sum 15, 9 sum 13; twice is 14, 16, 18: none fits

marks.rest: the factors of 7, 8 and 9 are added and the sums are written
marks.none: 2 x each number is written and each pair gets a cross

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step three, try seven, eight and nine to be sure. Their factors add up to eight, fifteen and thirteen.
<bookmark mark='none'/>Twice each is fourteen, sixteen and eighteen, so none of them fits.

marks.twice: 2 x 6 = 12 is written and the pair gets a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put six back. One plus two plus three plus six is twelve.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>Twelve is two times six, so six obeys the rule.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The perfect number between one and ten is six.
